title: SOFR Rate Observation - April 17, 2026
summary: SOFR closed at 3.65% on April 17, 2026, down 2 basis points from the prior day's reading of 3.67%. The rate has oscillated within a narrow 9 bps band (3.63% to 3.72%) over the most recent five trading days, indicating stable short-term dollar funding conditions.
key_points: Data source: FRED series SOFR, snapshot date 2026-04-20
why_it_matters: SOFR is the primary overnight dollar funding benchmark, replacing LIBOR across trillions of dollars in derivatives, loans, and floating-rate notes. Daily movements reflect underlying repo market conditions and short-term dollar liquidity. The narrow recent range suggests orderly funding markets absent of acute stress.
market_structure_context: SOFR (Secured Overnight Financing Rate) is derived from trades in the Treasury General Collateral repo market and serves as the overnight risk-free reference rate for dollar-denominated instruments. The rate's stability near 3.65% reflects benign short-term funding conditions. As the primary replacement for LIBOR, SOFR anchors pricing for interest rate swaps, floating-rate debt, and money market fund benchmarks.
